items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-08-06
items.q: And that's the one that Claude Kennedy went to. Yeah, I don't know the Oleana.

ctx.x: Back to Texas, were there many bands around Austin?

No, the biggest bands there was Troy, that is the Negro bands you're referring to, right? Either way. Well, I can't vividly remember the big white bands. One of them I remember was Furman Walden, and then it was Troy and it was Trent. Those were the names. Of course, we had the Oleana Orchestra in Galveston. And that's the one that Claude Kennedy went to. Yeah, I don't know the Oleana. No, it didn't last long.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-05-27
items.q: I took his place in Troy Floyd's band.

ctx.x: Well what about his style then? Beautiful. Great style. Did he sound the same as he did on the record with, say, LATER in 32?

I think he sounded better. I think he sounded better in person. One man that they weren't able to capture, I don't think, I've never heard anything from him, was Claude Benno Kennedy. I took his place in Troy Floyd's band. But he was not a powerful trumpet player.
Oh, yes. I knew him. Very much in Chicago.

That's right. Well, Lee was playing in the same neighborhood. And that's when Troy Floyd came to town. And I was a fellow who always liked to follow musicians. And I happened to go to a party I was having there for Troy. Troy was a great man then. And I got to talking to some of the guys in his band and also Trent's band. So Chester Clark, which is another great trumpet player, said, why don't you try to get that job with Troy's band? He says, Claude Kennedy's leaving. Oh, I says, I don't know if I could play…
After having that self-edged training for a year and a half, that comes to see for you.
